extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 49 476 participants (annual screening arm: 25 669 men; usual care arm: 23 807 men) aged 55 to 74 years were enrolled from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Study between the years 1993 and 2001.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared with the low tertile total fiber intake, high tertile total fiber intake in the annual screening arm was linked to reduced prostate cancer risk (adjusted hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.99), and high-soluble fiber intake in the usual care arm had a similar association (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.98) after adjusting for confounders.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Compared with the low tertile total fiber intake, high tertile total fiber intake in the annual screening arm was linked to reduced prostate cancer risk (adjusted hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.99), and high-soluble fiber intake in the usual care arm had a similar association (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.98) after adjusting for confounders.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Compared with the low tertile total fiber intake, high tertile total fiber intake in the annual screening arm was linked to reduced prostate cancer risk (adjusted hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.99), and high-soluble fiber intake in the usual care arm had a similar association
extraction_supporting_text.design: This study was a secondary analysis of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Study, a multicenter randomized trial conducted in the United States
extraction_supporting_text.timing: aged 55 to 74 years were enrolled from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Study between the years 1993 and 2001
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Cox proportional hazard and competing risk regressions were used within each arm to examine the associations of dietary fiber intake with prostate cancer risk
